standard.title: Plan, transact and negotiate with peers
standard.description: engage in activities that involve planning, transacting and negotiating with peers, using a range of phrases, sentences and structures and features
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can initiate and sustain exchanges using culturally appropriate conventions (AC9LCH8EC01). They can participate in digital and written interaction. They have not yet engaged in structured collaborative planning, transactional exchanges, or bilingual community-facing production in an academic context.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students engage in activities involving planning, transacting and negotiating with peers — including cultural events, transactions, collaborative projects, and bilingual community resources.

nodes.label: Collaborative planning and cultural event organisation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can collaborate with peers to plan cultural events or school activities, making decisions, negotiating roles, and using target language throughout.
nodes.minimum_width: Contribute to planning at least one event or activity in target language, making at least two planning decisions and justifying at least one.
nodes.typical_width: Plan Chinese cultural days and community events; organise class or school celebrations — explaining cultural practices and comparing with Australian practices; design group projects using research and personal experience; negotiate event formats, promotion strategies and participant roles.
wider: Lead the planning of a cultural event — coordinating decisions, managing peer input, and driving the group to a shared outcome using target language
Compare how community events are organised and promoted in target language community contexts versus Australian school contexts — identify the cultural differences in planning conventions
nodes.hinge_reason: Collaborative planning in target language is the prerequisite for all subsequent community-facing production and negotiation. Students who cannot sustain target language through a planning process cannot participate in the collaborative projects and bilingual resource creation this descriptor requires.

response_modes.reason: Collaborative planning requires students to contribute reasoned positions — not only preferences — and to manage competing views toward a shared outcome. Explicit planning task structures with justification requirements build this capacity.

success_criteria: Contributes at least two planning decisions in target language
Justifies at least one decision with a reason

nodes.label: Transactional and negotiating language
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can make real or simulated transactions — purchasing, requesting services, planning itineraries — negotiating details and reaching decisions as a group.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in at least one transactional or negotiating exchange, using target language to make a request, bargain or negotiate a detail, and reach a conclusion.
nodes.typical_width: Make real or simulated transactions — buying goods, requesting services, bargaining on price, planning itineraries; negotiate with peers about purchases and decisions based on collective opinions; provide metalanguage-supported peer feedback on spoken or written texts.
wider: Conduct a transactional exchange in a genuinely unfamiliar context — for example, booking a service or negotiating a complex arrangement — demonstrating flexible deployment of transactional language
Compare transactional language conventions in the target language with Australian English — identify differences in directness, bargaining conventions, and closing formulas

response_modes.reason: Transactional language must work across varied scenarios — shopping, services, itinerary planning, group decisions. Practising across different transaction types builds flexible deployment.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background language learner entry students may already conduct transactions in the target language in community contexts. Width investment here formalises and extends this authentic experience — building conscious command of transactional structures they may use implicitly.
success_criteria: Participates in a transactional exchange using target language to make a request or negotiate
Reaches a conclusion or decision through the exchange

nodes.label: Bilingual community-facing production
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create bilingual promotional or informational materials for community audiences, and produce resources to help others.
nodes.minimum_width: Create at least one bilingual resource (promotional material, helpful guide, or community information) that accurately conveys meaning in both languages for a specific audience.
nodes.typical_width: Produce bilingual promotional materials for community events; create resources for Chinese-speaking families to engage with school activities; produce helpful guides for other students; collaborate to create displays and performances for school and community audiences.
wider: Create a bilingual resource for a real community need — evaluate it with a target audience member and revise based on feedback
Design an 'ideal school' or community initiative with peers — drawing on research and own cultural experience to compare aspects across Australian and Chinese-speaking contexts

response_modes.reason: Bilingual community production integrates collaborative planning (node 1) and transactional language (node 2) into a genuine community-facing task. The teaching investment is in creating real community audiences — actual events, real family and community contexts — that give the production task authentic purpose.

success_criteria: Creates a bilingual resource with accurate meaning transfer in both languages
The resource is appropriate for its specified community audience
